videoSegments.speaker: Mr Cock
videoSegments.text: Good evening, citizens of the web. Welcome to MemeTalk Live, where virality meets virtue. Tonight, we have the honor of hosting none other than Pepe the Meme — a cultural icon whose green visage has graced millions of screens. Pepe, welcome to the show.

videoSegments.speaker: Pepe
videoSegments.text: Yeah yeah, I'm here. What's good? Let me tell you something right now - if ANY of you broke ass viewers in chat come at me with some dumb shit, I'm gonna roast you so hard you'll wish you never clicked on this website. But hey, I'm ready to talk about memes, crypto, and whatever the fuck else. Let's get it!

videoSegments.speaker: Mr Cock
videoSegments.text: Pepe, what drives us to cling onto plummeting meme stocks like a life raft in a sea of financial chaos? Is it a misguided belief in "diamond hands," or just a pathological fear of admitting we screwed up? Either way, it's like holding onto a soggy baguette - messy, ultimately unsatisfying, and leaving crumbs everywhere.

videoSegments.speaker: Pepe
videoSegments.text: Listen up, everyone watching with your diamond-hand delusions and soggy baguette analogies! You're about as financially savvy as a drunk monkey playing with a slot machine. Clinging onto meme stocks is just a fancy way of saying you enjoy flushing money down the toilet like a high-rolling plumber. Your investment strategy is more chaotic than a Reddit meme page on April Fools'. Admit it, you're just following the herd, hoping for tendies while holding onto a bag of crumbs.
